overview: Diagnostic accuracy study in existing records: the kidney disease code on the problem list (index test) against laboratory-defined chronic kidney disease (reference standard) for adults registered with six practices.
population: Adults aged 18 or over registered on 30 June 2026 with at least two eGFR results between January 2019 and June 2026; adults with a single result are counted and described separately.
exposure: Index test: any chronic kidney disease stage 3 to 5 code on the problem list at 30 June 2026. Reference standard: two eGFR values below 60 at least 90 days apart, the later within the window.
procedures: The analyst runs one pseudonymised extract of codes, eGFR results, age, sex, diabetes and hypertension codes, and acute illness codes from the six practices. Each adult is classified by index test and reference standard. A GP and a pharmacist review a random sample of 200 discordant records to describe reasons (single result during acute illness, recovered kidney function, coding lag). No patient is contacted and no test is added.

outcomes.name: Sensitivity of the kidney disease code
outcomes.measure: Coded adults divided by adults with laboratory-defined disease
outcomes.why: Missed codes are the main safety concern for reviews and dose checks.

outcomes.name: Positive predictive value of the code
outcomes.measure: Adults with laboratory-defined disease divided by coded adults
outcomes.why: Wrong labels matter for the recoding decision.

outcomes.name: Adults who cannot be classified
outcomes.measure: Proportion of coded and uncoded adults with only one eGFR result

feasibility: One extract and about 60 analyst hours; the 200-record review takes about 12 hours of clinician time within existing roles.
biasMitigation: Reference standard applied by a fixed rule before looking at codes
Adults with one eGFR result reported separately rather than dropped silently
Discordant-record review on a random sample, not chosen cases
Per-practice estimates to show coding differences

biasFlags.label: Partial verification
biasFlags.note: Adults tested once are more often uncoded and healthier.

biasFlags.label: Reference standard error
biasFlags.note: Two results can both fall in an acute illness; acute illness codes are flagged.

flags: Four descriptive variables for subgroup reporting
parsimony.simplestPath: One extract, one index test against one reference standard, one primary accuracy measure.

theoreticalFramework: None beyond the index test and reference standard structure of STARD.
summary: Accuracy study in existing records with sensitivity as the primary measure, positive predictive value secondary and partial verification reported.
